TheInterviewChair.com

Patent candidate list

Prepared for patent counsel · 2026-09-09
Following our call, here's the full list of everything we think may be worth evaluating — cast wide rather than pre-filtered, per your own steer that the combination is often where the real argument lives, not any single ingredient.
Context from our call: the sausage-machine example stuck with us — the meat guy and the skin guy both being individually "nothing new" doesn't stop the machine that combines them into something neither could argue against. Several items below are exactly that shape: individually unremarkable pieces (an AI call, a video avatar, a scoring rubric) combined into a specific sequence or mechanism that, as far as we know, nobody else has assembled this way. We've flagged which items are live in the product today versus designed-but-not-yet-built, in case that distinction matters for filing strategy.

Seeing it in action

One real, complete session — start to finish — so the mechanism behind each numbered item below is something you can actually see rather than take on description alone.
Step 1 — Setup
The candidate names the role (or uploads a job spec), sets difficulty and length, and can name a CV for extra personalisation — every question that follows is generated against this, not drawn from a fixed bank.
Step 2 — Before it begins
Confirms who's conducting the interview — Amina and Wayne, both live — and offers "Go Deeper", the opt-in for dynamic follow-up probing.
→ related to items 3, 5
Step 3 — Mike, the recruitment consultant
A third, separate AI avatar frames the session before handing over to the two interviewers proper.
Step 4 — Two interviewers, one session
Amina (HR) and Wayne (technical) are both live, both on camera, at the same time — not a single interviewer, not a pre-recorded sequence.
→ item 1
Step 5 — A real question, live
Wayne asks a scenario question built specifically for "Software Architect". Note the button row: Repeat, Pause, Tell Me The Answer, Pass — and, in the sidebar, a live coaching tip and a percentile benchmark against other candidates who've faced this same role.
→ items 1, 4, 5
Step 6 — Scored and coached, immediately
Seconds after answering, the candidate gets specific coaching referencing exactly what they said — plus a live breakdown across four independent scoring dimensions (relevance, clarity, depth, confidence), before the next question even loads.
→ items 6, 7
Step 7 — The bonus round
A surprise knowledge check fires mid-interview, in character, with a full worked explanation regardless of the answer chosen.
→ items 2, 8
Step 8 — Session complete
The candidate chooses whether this session gets kept — nothing is published without an explicit decision here.
Step 9 — Broadcast, not just saved
Saving generates a shareable link and a scannable QR code the candidate can paste directly onto a CV — this is the "broadcast" in the product's name. Note "Public — visible in Candidate Search": the same recording also enters the searchable pool.
→ items 13, 14, 16
Step 10 — Every session, individually controlled
The full history: 23 saved interviews, 11 of them public. Every row carries its own score, its own recording, and its own visibility switch — a candidate can search across roles and companies, and flip any single interview private again at any time, or use the bulk "Interview Visibility" control to change all of them at once.
→ item 16
Step 11 — What the recruiter actually sees
Scanning that QR code opens the full interview replay on any phone, with every question timestamped and clickable — a recruiter watches the actual session, not a summary of it.
→ item 13
Step 12 — Or a recruiter finds you first
The other direction: a recruiter searches the Candidate Marketplace directly and gets back real candidates with real scores from real completed interviews — this is what "searchable" actually means in practice, not a hypothetical.
→ item 14
Step 13 — Where you fell short becomes exactly what you study
A real low-scoring moment: 37% on ASP.NET Core, with the specific dimension that let it down (Depth, 5%) visible in the breakdown. "Study ASP.NET Core →" isn't a generic link — it carries the exact topic the candidate just struggled with.
→ item 11
Step 14 — Straight into a fresh course on exactly that
That click lands here with the topic already filled in — one more click generates a full course on the precise thing the interview just showed was weak, at a difficulty the candidate chooses. The loop closes without the candidate ever having to type the topic themselves.
→ items 9, 11

01Interview delivery & format

The live interview session itself — how it's conducted, not how it's scored.
1.Dual concurrent real-time AI interviewer avatarsLive
Two independent, simultaneously-connected real-time video AI avatars — one HR-focused, one technical-role-focused — conduct one continuous interview session, handing off between each other live based on which question is being asked, rather than a single interviewer or a pre-recorded/sequential avatar.
Possible angle: the concurrent dual-session architecture itself, and the live handoff logic between two independently-running AI personas within one interview.
2.Mid-interview cinematic knowledge checkLive
A surprise multiple-choice knowledge test is woven directly into the flow of a live interview at a scripted moment (not a separate quiz module), introduced and reacted to by the AI interviewer in character, with correct answers adding bonus points that lift the candidate's overall interview score.
Possible angle: knowledge-testing embedded inside — and mathematically affecting the outcome of — a conversational interview simulation, rather than run as a separate assessment.
3.AI-decided dynamic follow-up probingLive
The same AI call that scores a candidate's answer also decides, in that same pass, whether the answer sounds too generic or unverifiable to be genuine — and if so, generates and puts to the candidate live (spoken, by the avatar) a specific follow-up question probing for a concrete detail. Aggressiveness scales with a selected difficulty tier.
Possible angle: an automated, real-time "detect a rehearsed or shallow answer and probe it live" mechanism, folded into the same scoring pass rather than a separate step.
4."Tell Me The Answer" reveal with structural anti-cheat lockLive
A candidate who doesn't know an answer can request a full AI-generated worked model answer instead of guessing or passing blind. The system speaks the answer aloud, in the same interviewer voice, rather than just displaying text. The interface makes it structurally impossible to then read that answer back as their own attempt — the reveal is a blocking state whose only exit immediately advances to the next question — and usage is tracked and reported as a distinct metric, separate from genuine scored attempts.
Possible angle: the specific UI lock that prevents reveal-then-recite, combined with treating "asked to learn it" as a first-class, separately-tracked outcome type alongside pass/answer.
5.Candidate-directed topic focus ("With special focus on")Live
An optional field alongside the job title at intake. A "What's Hot" button AI-generates 3-4 currently in-demand subjects for that exact job title (e.g. "Agentic AI Patterns", "Zero Trust Architecture" for a Software Architect role); the candidate keeps, discards, or replaces any of them, and can type their own topics directly too. Whatever survives that curation is woven into the AI's question generation, replacing default generic/CV-inferred questions with hard, targeted questions on those exact topics, and the technical interviewer explicitly names one or two of them out loud in his own spoken intro — a deterministic, guaranteed acknowledgement, not left to chance.
Possible angle: AI-suggested, then candidate-curated, topic selection — the suggestion is a starting point, not the final input, and only what the candidate actively chooses to keep shapes the actual interview content and gets spoken back to them by name.

02Scoring, coaching & results

What happens to an answer after it's given.
6.Multi-dimensional real-time answer scoringLive
Each answer is scored live across independent dimensions (clarity, relevance, depth, confidence) plus a blended overall score, combined in the same pass with voice-delivery metrics — speaking pace in words-per-minute and filler-word detection — captured from the same spoken answer.
Possible angle: combining content-quality scoring and delivery-quality scoring from one spoken input into one unified real-time result.
7.In-session personalized AI coachingLive
Immediately after an answer is scored, a second AI pass generates specific coaching feedback that references the candidate's own answer, their CV, and the target job specification — delivered before the next question, not as a batch report at the end.
Possible angle: real-time, three-way-contextualised (answer + CV + job spec) coaching delivered mid-session rather than post-hoc.
8.Blended bonus-and-core scoring modelLive
Bonus points from the mid-interview knowledge check (item 2) mathematically lift the same headline score the core interview answers produce, rather than being reported as a disconnected side-note next to an unaffected percentage.
Possible angle: a single unified scoring formula spanning two structurally different assessment types (open-ended answers and multiple-choice) within one session.

03Learning & retention mechanic

The Learn Engine — using the interview format for general studying, not just job prep.
9.General-purpose "study via interview" methodLive
For any subject a user types in — not limited to job-interview preparation — the system AI-generates a full structured lesson (concepts, glossary, exam questions) and then interviews the user on that freshly-generated material, deliberately using the interview/testing format itself as the retention mechanic.
Possible angle: applying a job-interview-style conversational testing format as a general study technique for arbitrary subjects, with the lesson content itself freshly AI-generated per topic rather than drawn from a fixed curriculum.
10."Micro-subject" as the core discoverable unitLive
Hyper-specific study/practice topics (e.g. "Deploy a .NET app to Azure") are treated as the platform's primary searchable and shareable unit, rather than broad subject categories.
Possible angle: the granularity choice itself as the addressable/shareable content unit, distinct from how competitors structure course or topic taxonomies.
11.Interview-performance-driven, auto-generated targeted study contentLive
Every missed multiple-choice question and every below-threshold scored answer on a completed interview carries its own "Study this →" action, which routes directly into the Learn Engine (item 9) and AI-generates a fresh, full lesson on that exact topic — closing the loop from a genuine interview performance signal straight into targeted study material generated specifically for that gap, rather than a generic course catalogue or a self-selected topic list.
Possible angle: using real assessment performance data, not a quiz or self-reported skill gap, as the direct trigger for freshly-generated, topic-specific learning content — the diagnostic (the interview) and the remediation (the lesson) are produced by the same underlying generation mechanism.
12.Aggregate course assembly from every flagged weak areaPlanned, not yet built
Extending item 11 from one topic at a time to a single, full course automatically assembled from every weak area flagged across a candidate's interview history at once, rather than requiring one click per gap.
Possible angle: a multi-source diagnostic (many interviews, many flagged competencies) feeding one synthesized curriculum, rather than a single quiz result mapping to a single pre-built course.

04Distribution & matching

How a completed interview reaches employers.
13.Record-once, broadcast-to-many distributionLive
A candidate completes one AI-conducted interview once, then distributes it to potentially many recruiters and employers simultaneously via a persistent shareable link and scannable QR code — replacing the need to repeat the same live interview separately for each employer.
Possible angle: this is close to the core "world's first Interview Broadcast Platform" positioning — the one-to-many distribution of a single AI-conducted interview session, as opposed to one-to-one video interviewing tools.
14.Searchable pool of live-recorded interviewsLive
Every completed, opted-in interview recording becomes part of a pool recruiters and employers can search directly — by role, score, and competency — rather than relying only on push-based alerts (item 15) or a traditional keyword search over static CV text. The searchable unit is the actual interview recording and its structured scoring data, not a self-written summary of it.
Possible angle: search built directly on top of real completed interview sessions and their AI-generated scoring, as the primary discovery mechanism, rather than on CVs or profile text.
15.Two-sided live matching / alert engineLive
Recruiters and employers set standing criteria ("notify me when a candidate scores above X for role Y") that fire in real time as new interviews complete. Candidates simultaneously see a live feed of demand signals matching their own profile — a bidirectional system rather than one-directional job-board search. The score an alert matches against is the same blended figure from item 2 — MCQ bonus points included — not just the raw core-answer average, so a strong bonus-round performance can itself be what tips a candidate over an alert's threshold.
Possible angle: the symmetry — both sides get live, standing, criteria-based push notifications from the same underlying event, rather than one side searching a static listing — combined with the alert firing off the same composite score (core answers + knowledge-check bonus) rather than a single isolated number.
16.Reversible per-interview visibility with bulk toggleLive
A candidate can publish or unpublish any individual completed interview — or all of them at once — for recruiter discovery at any time after the fact, rather than a one-way "submit" action that can't be undone.
Possible angle: narrower than most items here, but the reversibility itself (versus every competing platform's one-way submission model) is a deliberate, arguably non-obvious design choice.

05Cost-efficient personalization at scale

Making expensive AI generation affordable per-candidate.
17.Shared personalized-greeting cache keyed by first nameLive
A synthesized, lip-synced "Hi [Name]" video greeting moment is generated once per first name and reused for every candidate who shares that name, rather than regenerating an expensive personalized video clip per individual candidate.
Possible angle: a specific caching architecture that makes personalized AI video economically viable at scale — the "key by first name, not by person" choice is the actual mechanism, not just "we cache things".

06Platform & access architecture

Weaker candidates than the above — more conventional engineering — included per your instruction to send everything.
18.Single neutral role-routing authentication gateLive
One shared login/registration entry point authenticates a user once and routes them into the correct one of several otherwise-independent applications (candidate, recruiter, employer, admin) based on their role, rather than each portal running its own separate authentication silo.
Possible angle: likely the weakest item on this list — single sign-on with role routing is a common pattern — but included since the specific "neutral gate" implementation across genuinely separate applications may still be worth a look.
19.Business-plan pitch as a formal interview typePlanned, not yet built
Treating a founder's business plan pitch as its own interview type, run through the same AI scoring/coaching apparatus (multi-dimensional scoring, live coaching, follow-up probing) built for job interviews.
Possible angle: extending the same underlying interview-and-score mechanism to a materially different use case (pitching, not job-seeking) — the transferability of the mechanism itself may be worth protecting ahead of building it.
20.Spoken "tell me about this role" career guideLive
A "Tell Me About This Role" button on any career page has the same interviewer voice read the role aloud — salary bands, automation-risk score, career timeline, and other structured data for that specific role — narrated as a natural spoken answer rather than a static content page the candidate has to read themselves. Built as a deterministic script templated from the role's own structured data, not an AI-generated answer and not personalized to the individual candidate's CV.
Possible angle: reusing the same voice/avatar apparatus built for interviewing to narrate structured career-market data as a spoken answer, rather than building a separate static content page for it — the interview interface itself doubling as a career-research tool.

07Aggregate market intelligence

A byproduct of item 5's curation step — a real, cross-candidate dataset, not a single candidate's data.
21.Cross-candidate "in-demand subjects" dataset from real curation choicesLive
Every topic a candidate actually keeps (not just what the AI suggested) from item 5's "What's Hot" step is logged against that job title, aggregated across every candidate who has ever interviewed for that role — one running counter per (role, subject) pair, not a raw per-candidate log. A query for any job title returns the subjects real candidates have judged worth practicing, ranked by how often they were kept, ready to feed public-facing reporting or back into the AI's own future question-generation prompts.
Possible angle: the underlying signal is a real human decision (keep vs. discard an AI suggestion), aggregated at scale into a dataset about what a job market actually cares about — distinct from both a single candidate's data and from the AI's own unverified suggestion, since only what candidates chose to keep counts.
This list was compiled by reviewing the actual live product and its architecture — it's a starting inventory for evaluation, not a claim that any item here is in fact novel or non-obvious in the legal sense. Happy to go deeper on the technical mechanism behind any item, or pull supporting detail (dates first built, any prior art we're aware of) on request.
